Three bugs no review pass could have found

Six phases were each reviewed on their own diff, then the whole epic got one more integration-level /pr-review pass. All of that is static analysis and reading code. None of it boots the application. These three only exist at the seam between "the code is correct" and "the code runs" — and a live boot found all three within the first few minutes.

1 · Dockerfile never learned @openlinker/integrations-fx exists

The image build hand-enumerates every @openlinker/* workspace package for layer-caching COPY steps — a list the Dockerfile's own comment warns about by name ("the #1365 review class of bug"). The new FX package was never added to it, in any of six phases. docker build failed outright: ERR_PNPM_WORKSPACE_PKG_NOT_FOUND.

Fix: three one-line additions to the Dockerfile's manifest and dist COPY lists.

2 · OL_REPORTING_CURRENCY was set on the API service, not the worker

Caught by the final /pr-review pass, not by booting — but only because that review specifically traced which process actually runs ingestion. Order ingestion, the retry job and the hourly sweep all run in the worker, and the settings resolution's env fallback is per-process. The demo compose set the PLN default only under api:, so a fresh deployment would have silently stamped in EUR (the code-constant default) until an operator opened the settings page — directly contradicting the compose file's own comment.

Fix: mirror the same env var into the worker: service block.

3 · The migration's own unit test crashed the migration

This is the one only a live boot could ever have found — nothing short of actually running migration:run against a database exercises this path.

TypeORM's CLI discovers migrations by globbing migrations/**/*{.ts,.js} and require()s every match directly as a migration module. The FX migration shipped with a colocated unit spec at migrations/__tests__/…add-order-fx-stamp.spec.ts — a genuinely good idea (it verifies the CHECK constraint's SQL by parsing and evaluating it, since Testcontainers never runs a real migration). But the CLI glob swept it up too, and hit a bare describe(…) outside of Jest:

ReferenceError: describe is not defined

Every migrate run on this branch exited 1. No order table changes, no app boot.

Fix: moved the spec to database/__tests__/, beside data-source.ts (the file that owns the glob) and outside its reach. Jest's repo-wide testRegex still finds it there — no test-discovery change, just a location the CLI never walks.

The live stamp, verified by hand

Once all three fixes landed, the migration ran clean against a real Postgres, the API registered both rate providers at boot, and — after manually triggering the hourly reconcile sweep instead of waiting for its cron tick — the worker made a genuine HTTP call to NBP's public reference-rate API and wrote the first stamp.

✓ Checked by hand: 19.99 × 4.342 = 86.79658, which rounds to exactly the 86.80 the database holds. The direction invariant holds too — this multiplies, never divides, exactly as ADR-040 requires.

The registry deduplicates correctly, live

By the time this report was written, 8 of 81 orders were stamped — but only 4 rows exist in exchange_rates. Multiple orders placed on the same day share one NBP lookup, exactly as the registry's (source, from, to, rateDate) key was designed to guarantee. The sweep was still running when this snapshot was taken, which is why the count keeps climbing rather than jumping straight to 81 — bounded per-tick processing, also by design.
